task_instance: Migrate a small sample Expo native module (EchoModule.swift: a module with a Name, a Constant, a sync Function, an async Function, and an Event) from the Expo Modules API 1.0 definition() DSL to the 2.0 macro API (@ExpoModule/@JS/@Event), preserving the JS contract.
blocker_detail: The skill's workflow requires (step 4) building/type-checking the Apple/Swift module against expo-modules-core, running native unit tests, and building+launching the example iOS app in Xcode to confirm the migrated macro code actually compiles, links, and that expo-module.config.json still resolves the module at runtime. Apple's Swift/Xcode toolchain and iOS SDKs are macOS-only and cannot be installed or run on this Linux container (no `swift`/`swiftc`, no Xcode, no CocoaPods build environment; `apt-get install swift` resolves to the unrelated OpenStack Swift package, and there is no path to obtain a real Apple toolchain on Linux). I could write the source-level migration (1.0 DSL -> 2.0 macro syntax) by hand from documented knowledge of the macro API, but could not compile, type-check, run tests, or launch the example app, so the actual deliverable (a verified, building, contract-preserving migrated module) could not be produced or confirmed. Additionally, the skill's own references/migration-map.md, references/example.md and references/compatibility.md (which it says must be read before changing source) are not present in the skill's source directory, so even the mapping rules had to be reconstructed from general knowledge rather than the skill's stated reference material.

Wrote a sample 1.0-DSL module at sample-module/ios/EchoModule.swift and a hand-written 2.0 macro migration at sample-module/ios/EchoModule.migrated.swift preserving the module name, constant, sync/async function signatures and threading behavior, and event name.
